problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-v⟩$ at the point $(1,1,2).$
worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(1,1,2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ {v}^{2}=1 \\ {u}^{2}-v=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) & =⟨0,\,2(-1),\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,1,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
